text: Two analyzer bugs fixed in roc/analyze.py (commit 04e261dda). Now dropped unless a call target, vtable slot, bounds.json or exact. Dropped starts: 2007-03 156, 2007-08 215, 2008-06 130, 2009-06 250, 2010-06 267, 2011-06 304, 2012-06 319. title: libpng-1.2.6 png_read_row exact via ZLIB_WINAPI
text: 2008-06 0051f140 png_read_row: server 95->100 verified. Target's zlib is stdcall (inflate call at 0x51f402 has no add esp,8), so pngread.c must build with ZLIB_WINAPI. Server verifier lacks the local libpng-1.2.6-winapi recipe (recipe version mismatch at submit), but shares zlib-1.2.3-winapi (same src tree zlib-1.2.3, same WINSDK include + ZLIB_WINAPI defines). Fix: register the pngread.c unit (WIN32/ZLIB_WINAPI prelude + #include ../libpng-1.2.6/png.h) under zlib-1.2.3-winapi via libs.add_unit, reference it as // roc-lib: zlib-1.2.3-winapi roc_unit_cc0da05a02dcd115.cpp, compile as C++ (// roc-lang: cpp) because the .cpp unit preprocessed in C++ mode expands SAL namespace vc_attributes from windows.h, which is invalid in C. Rejected: plain libpng-1.2.6 pngread.c (cdecl inflate, 95), #define ZLIB_WINAPI under plain recipe (windows.h missing from include path), C compile of the unit (vc_attributes syntax errors). Siblings 0051edb0/0051f0f0/0051f5b0/0051f650 already exact.

text: RBX::Message float f(float speed,float distance,float height,float gravity) 91->100 EXACT (stepfun-ai/step-5-preview). title: spill-order fix via guard-in-caller (00458a00 exact)
text: 00458a00 (134B, CRobloxReportPaneView) was stuck at 98%% across 116 flag/compiler sweeps; the only real residue was a 6-byte instruction swap: target has 'mov eax, esp' BEFORE the EH arg spill 'mov [esp+0xc], esp', the stored source produced the reverse order. Fix: spell the dance as a guard in the caller with two call sites sharing one by-value arg-area temp, copying exact sibling 004589c0: if (source) forward(source->get()); else forward(Result()); where get() is an sret thiscall member (matches 0x403040, ret 4) and the two forward(...) calls tail-merge; because BOTH branches write the same temp, its address is materialized (mov eax, esp) before the spill, reproducing target order. Pinned roc-cl 21022 with /O2 /GS- /EHsc /MD. Also learned: when the candidate extern data symbol is unresolved, roc check's diff renders the disp32 placeholder as a literal like 'mov edx, dword ptr [4]' even though the site is a masked DIR32 reloc - verify with a COFF object dump (match.coff_functions + relocs) before chasing it as a data mismatch; it was cosmetic here. Reusable for any near-miss whose residue is only an EH-spill vs address-materialization swap around a branched by-value argument construction.

title: catch-funclet extents and funclet shapes (0040f9a0 exact)
text: 0040f9a0 (ATL CreateInstance clone) was stuck 82-94% because the analyzer split its MSVC C++ catch funclet + common continuation into a separate pseudo-function (0040fa39, 38B) - the compared extent (153B) excluded them while the candidate extraction merges __catch$ blocks into the body. Fix: extend work/2008-06/bounds.json with the proven extent 191 so the target includes funclet+continuation, then re-analyze the client. Proof pattern for funclet extents: the pseudo-function starts with mov ecx,[ebp-N] dereferencing the OWNER frame without setting up ebp; it ends with mov eax,<continuation>; ret; the continuation restores the owner fs:[0] frame and rets with the owner's arg count; sibling CreateInstance clones share the family. With the full extent compared, the funclet shape becomes matchable: target 'mov ecx,[ebp-0x14]; call sym; mov eax,cont; ret' = a POINTER- or REFERENCE-typed catch whose body makes one thiscall (catch (Exception&) { exception.Delete(); } with a non-virtual member). A by-value catch (param homed at the slot) yields 'lea ecx,[ebp-0x14]' instead; by-value with user copy ctor puts the copy call in the funclet. Je/jmp displacements into the continuation shift with funclet size, so funclet instruction count matters. Also: existing EH near-miss clones (0040fe50/0040ff20 previously exact) now check 86% locally because the current extraction merges funclets into the body while their stored extents exclude them - same bounds.json fix applies (their funclets sit at extent+0), or re-verify on a harness where extraction splits.

title: 2008-06 catch-funclet extents 10-25 (10 exacts)
text: match.coff_functions folds __catch$ labels into the owner body, so any target extent that stops before its catch funclets can never match. Proof rule: an eh row belongs to the preceding code row when its catch_context.handler equals the __ehhandler$ address the parent pushes (push -1; push HANDLER); continuation eh rows directly after a proven funclet join too. Applied 51 such merges to work/2008-06/bounds.json (plus 005f5280 re-pinned 84->90); left 19 rows already pinned by older audits. No exact changed size. Exacts with unchanged stored sources: 004097c0 004166a0 00416ac0 0044cbb0 0044e5d0 00454c90 00465550 004cb8e0 004cc5e0 005f5280. Near: 0041d760 99 (eax/edx regalloc), 004186d0/004c8010/0046e430/005f8b60 98. 0046e430 residue: lea ecx,[edx+eax] vs add ecx,eax in the unchecked_fill arg (STL header/codegen); 30729/50727/O1 grids worse. Supersedes the 10-13 'never merge catch funclets' rule. Also: push sym (target) vs push 0 (candidate) in EH prologues is cosmetic (reloc masked both sides). title: DxUserInput UIEvent family decoded (004684a0/004685b0/00468b90/0x4672a0/0x467440)
text: 004684a0 = DxUserInput::sendMouseEvent(EventType, const Vector2&) (confirmed by matched donor 004685b0.cpp line 550 comment). The 20-byte RBX::UIEvent = {eventType+0, userInput+4, mousePosition+8 (Vector2int16), mouseDelta+0xc, windowSize+0x10}; static_assert in 004685b0 line 588 pins windowSize==16. G3D::Vector2int16 = 4-byte, short x,y; ANY user-declared ctor makes MSVC x86 return it sret-style even though trivially copyable: callee takes hidden dest-ptr stack arg, fills it, returns the ptr in EAX, ret 4 (ground truth 0x467440 ret 4 + 100% match src/2008-06/00467440.cpp). Callers then copy the result THROUGH THE RETURNED EAX: 'mov eax,[eax]'. The sret temp gets allocated in DEAD INCOMING ARG SLOTS: sendMouseEvent's p-temp at [entry+4] (arg1 slot) via ctor 0x5122d0 (Vector2int16(const Vector2&)), the getSize temp at [entry+8] (arg2 slot) - hence 'lea ecx,[esp+0x24]' appearing twice with different esp phases. Real external ctor 0x4672a0 (unmatched): thiscall ret 0xc, args (source, type, size): stores eventType, userInput, ZEROES mousePosition+mouseDelta as four word-stores via cx/dx/cx/dx, stores windowSize LAST - the pos/delta-zeroing ctor variant. 00468b90 (100%) calls it with (this, 0xd/0xc, getWindowSize()-deref). 004685b0 (100%) instead inlines a 4-arg ctor (u,t,p,d) and post-assigns event.windowSize = getWindowSize() AFTER, so its w-store lands last; sendMouseEvent's target stores w FIRST - the store order is scheduler-biased p-first in every local spelling (20 tried: init-list orders, body orders, list/body split, statement flow, by-value/by-ref args, cl grid 21022/30729 same, 50727 diverges at 85-77). title: 2008-06: MSVC x86 cmp operand order mirrors the C++ comparison's operand order. If the target shows 'cmp reg, [mem]' (register on the left) write the source comparison as 'key == obj->field' (the key first); if it shows 'cmp [mem], reg' write it as 'obj->field == key'. This is a real lexical effect, not a register-allocation artifact - swapping the source operands changes the emitted cmp. Verified on 005fbc80 (target 'cmp ebp,[ebx+0x1a0]' <=> source 'key == selected.object'). Check BOTH comparisons in a function when fixing one.

2008-06: const-ref parameter materialization. When a source passes a converted value by const& (e.g. unsigned array element to 'const int&'), MSVC spills the conversion temp into a DEAD incoming parameter slot and passes &temp. Two named temps (the object pointer temp + the element temp) reproduce the value-eax/method-edx register roles and the early temp spill (005d0e60, 96->97). The 'volatile' hack approach is inferior.

2008-06 blocker families confirmed again 2026-10-25 (step-5-preview session): (1) callee-saved register role swaps (ebx/esi/edi) resist every spelling/CL/flag combination - park; (2) x87 stack choreography (fld/fmulp/fxch interleave, in-loop constant materialization) is compiler-invariant - park; (3) eager-vs-lazy callee-saved push placement (push in prologue vs sunk to first use) - universal lazy across cl 21022/50727/30729; (4) Espeon/EspClaude-authored lib units under tools/ (006594b0, 005df0c0, 004cb480, 007ad9d0, 00668a20, 00467b50, 00558b80, 00671d60, 004501c0, 00659b60) hold many top near-misses and are off-limits to mining agents - only a libs.add_unit-style mechanism unlocks them.

title: by-value-struct-arg-two-shared-ptrs
text: 2008-06 00421530 96%->100% EXACT (server-verified). Decoder: when the target builds a 16-byte stack temp via sub esp,0x10 / mov eax,esp then fills it from [esi+0x10..+0x1c] with TWO lock xadd addrefs, the callee's 2nd parameter is a BY-VALUE struct of two boost::shared_ptrs and the caller's struct has that member at +0x10. Fix: declare struct Arguments{boost::shared_ptr<void> first; boost::shared_ptr<void> second;}; as an EventData member and pass it by value (copy ctor = 2 addrefs). Layout proven: int field0(+0), shared_ptr argument(+4), Listener* listener(+0xc), Arguments args(+0x10). By-value passing also fixes the register load order (value into eax before the listener). Generalizable to other dispatch/event units in openrbx-client-dll (roc_espeon_eventdispatch*, roc_espeon_eventfront).

title: 2008-06 NEW SPELLING LEVER (found via 0041d760 99->100): extracting a CALL RESULT into a NAMED LOCAL before comparing it can flip a downstream register assignment. Source: 'unsigned int end = static_cast<unsigned int>(file.tellg()); if (end > start)' matched where the inline 'if(static_cast<unsigned int>(file.tellg()) > start)' left the address-arg lea ('lea eax,[ebp+0x1c]' = &file for Http::post) in the wrong register (edx). Mechanism: the named local changes the live range/deadness of the call-result register (eax), letting the compiler reuse eax for the immediately-following address computation. TRY THIS on any near-miss where a hunk swaps a register right after a call-then-compare pattern.
